paragraphs: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba (the priest). In Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Kirah, on the mishnah “A hot-water urn that he emptied,” etc.: Rabbi Ba, grandson of Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba. Perhaps this is a scribal error and should read “Rabbi Ba, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba.” Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi and Rabbi Acha (Ein Yaakov: Chama) bar Chanina disagree about it; one says, etc. Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, told them: “Thus said Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba in Rabbi Yochanan’s name” (Berakhot, first chapter, 5, end of a). He said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name (the source reads ת״ר יוחנן): Gittin 76b; Temurah 14b; Keitzad Mevarkhin 43b, 48a, 61b; Megillah 19b—several things. Rabbi Abba bar Chiyya bar Abba’s colleague learned it from him—who was it? Rabbi Zeira. Some say Rabbi Zeira’s colleague learned it from Rabbi Zeira—who was it? Rabbi Abba son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba (Mo'ed Katan 22a); see below, Rabbi Acha. Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Zeira learned from Rabbi Abba bar Chiyya. Rabbi Zeira called him “elder.” He was in the marketplace of Caesarea, Rabbi Abbahu’s locality; Rabbi Ammi was there [ר״י; abbreviation uncertain], and Rabbi Zeira told Rabbi Ammi, “You have not allowed us to ask the elder Rabbi Abba, who heard from his father Rabbi Chiyya, and Rabbi Chiyya from Rabbi Yochanan” (Chullin 86b). Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Yannai in Shabbat 121b. In Rabbah, beginning of Bechukkotai, section 35, he spoke in Rabbi Yonatan’s name. Rabbi Abba bar Chiyya raised a contradiction to Rabbi Abbahu, Tamid Nishchat 59b. He reported that Rabbi Yehudah Hanasi (Rashi: Rabbi’s grandson) ruled, but they did not agree with him (Avodah Zarah 37a).
